long_biography.plain_text:
A study tour of North American self-service stores gave Erwin Franz Müller a model for changing his hairdressing business. In its early mixed salon-and-drugstore phase, he delivered goods by car and used a laundry room as storage. Four years after the trip, he opened the first dedicated Müller drugstore.

Müller developed the chain around unusually wide assortments and its own logistics. Distribution centres and an in-house transport company supported expansion across European markets, while acquisitions added specialist retailers in toys, household goods and beauty. A larger executive team now shares operating responsibility while continuing to report to Müller.
